places: Full-page High Era panorama at civilization scale: multiple inhabited worlds linked by immense stable green corridors, with civilian, diplomatic, and freight traffic moving through luminous lanes around elegant Cooperative and BHA infrastructure. The age feels prosperous, precise, optimistic, and almost impossibly connected. No post-Shattering faction, uniform, ship class, or institution is present

Full-page view spanning polished Core infrastructure toward harder-used Outer Band systems. Most corridor lines remain luminous green, but faint timing echoes and tiny doubled traces are visible. Human-scale maintenance work continues while freight and medical cargo wait at the edges of an apparently functional network

Full-page layered infrastructure vista: immaculate civic and transit architecture above, massive older corridor machinery and service structures beneath, and distant outer maintenance platforms showing more wear. Everything is still operating, but the inherited system's age is physically visible

Full-page view centered on the immense dormant damping chamber, ancient enough to dwarf the small figures working near it. Corridor telemetry shows unstable load relationships while the chamber's old emitter systems are prepared for use

Full-page image inside the damping chamber: monumental emitters, layered old engineering, and tiny human figures working beneath machinery built for a more cautious age. Through apertures and instrument light, the still-vast High Era corridor network remains active above

Full-page deep-space corridor image: a ship traveling inside a once-clean route has a faint delayed duplicate silhouette displaced beside it, while beacon anchors and luminous lane geometry show visible misalignment. The effect is physical, measurable, and increasingly dangerous

Full-page civilization-scale corridor vista in active distortion: ships, ports, inhabited worlds, and logistics remain visible while luminous route geometry folds, slips, and disagrees with itself. Daily life is still moving inside the failure

Full-page post-collapse nightscape made of islands of human light: a damaged habitat braced by hand, a rough route board built from witness reports, supplies moving between local groups, and a newly painted safety mark whose use is still being negotiated

Full-page lived-world recovery scene: repaired structural bracing, water and heat distribution, a hand-verified route board, improvised cargo transfer, and a newly painted safety mark. Distinct local practices are visible without becoming formalized factions

Cross-cut montage between an Outer Ring repair deck, Orban-Tier Transit Port, and a rebuilt standards workspace: three distinct post-Break practices operating at the same time without sharing one visual language

Full-page view around the prototype rescue vessel on its gantry. Different crews contribute patched engineering, route data, annotated documents, and a shared safety sigil. The command position remains unassigned while the ship is made ready for launch

Full-page view of the nearly completed prototype rescue vessel surrounded by mixed crews and equipment from emerging post-Break traditions. The shared safety sigil is visible as a common operating mark, while the ship remains visibly improvised and transitional

Full-page departure vista: the prototype rescue vessel moves through fractured but usable routes accompanied by distinct escort groups. Their equipment, route practices, and crew organization remain visibly different even as they share one safety sigil

lighting.ceremony: High directional or stained-glass light with soft fill; faces readable and banners highlighted.
lighting.council: Even overhead illumination; consistent glow on central tables and displays.
lighting.engineering: Harsh task lighting with reflective metal surfaces and visible status indicators.
lighting.collapse: Unsteady emergency lighting, intermittent strobes, and partial power loss.
lighting.ritual: Soft perimeter glow with shallow shadows; calm, contemplative illumination.
